question: Should ClawHub retain behavior-based financial-content rules, or categorically exclude specified crypto, trading, wallet, payment, identity, registry, or reputation subcategories from the public registry?
rationale: Current main prohibits fraud, unsafe execution, deceptive publishing, and abusive behavior while evaluating legitimate powerful capabilities contextually; the RFC’s draft category-wide exclusion would materially change that product and security boundary.

options.title: Keep behavior-based rules
options.body: Allow legitimate financial and on-chain tools when transparent, purpose-aligned, and safety-bounded while blocking fraud, unsafe execution, and marketplace abuse.

options.title: Ban narrow high-risk classes
options.body: Categorically exclude clearly defined transaction, custody, or autonomous-spending workflows while preserving read-only, educational, identity, registry, and reputation uses.

options.title: Ban the full category
options.body: Exclude crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading content from the public registry regardless of implementation details.

recommendation.title: Keep behavior-based rules
recommendation.body: Allow legitimate financial and on-chain tools when transparent, purpose-aligned, and safety-bounded while blocking fraud, unsafe execution, and marketplace abuse.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC, are a repository collaborator, and have continued handling moderation-policy decisions in this area.
